paper.title: Thompson Sampling for Budgeted Multi-armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Budgeted MAB (Bernoulli and general bandits, rewards and costs in [0,1])
unmapped: Each pull yields a random reward and a random cost (both in [0,1], independent of each other); play stops when budget B is exhausted; regret measured against the optimal policy with known distributions, as a function of budget B
Optimal arm is the one with maximal expected-reward-to-expected-cost ratio; all mean rewards and costs are positive
settings.definition_quote: At round $t$, a player pulls an arm $i\in[K]$, receives a random reward $r_i(t)$, and pays a random cost $c_i(t)$ until he runs out of his budget $B$, which is a positive integer. Both the reward $r_i(t)$ and the cost $c_i(t)$ are supported on $[0,1]$.

symbols.Phi_i: O(1/eps_i^4) if mu_1^c+eps_i>=1, else O(1/(eps_i^6 (1-mu_1^c-eps_i))), with eps_i(gamma)=(1-gamma) mu_1^c Delta_i/(mu_i^r/mu_i^c+1)

conditions: rewards and costs supported in [0,1], reward independent of cost
mu_i^r > 0 and mu_i^c > 0 for all arms
B positive integer (proof uses B > e)

source.label: thm:bound_TS_asymp
source.quote: $\forall \gamma \in (0,1)$, for both Bernoulli bandits and general bandits, the regret of the BTS algorithm can be upper bounded as below. Regret \leq \sum_{i=2}^{K}\Big\{\frac{2\ln B}{\gamma^2\mu_i^c\Delta_i}\bigg(\frac{\mu_1^r}{\mu_1^c}+1\bigg)^2 + \Phi_i(\gamma)\Big\}+O\bigg(\frac{K}{\gamma^2}\bigg)

results.notes: Leading ln B term has explicit constants; remaining terms are O(.) with constants depending on the instance but not B. Holds for Bernoulli and general [0,1] bandits (Bernoulli is special case). Remark 4 instantiates gamma=1/sqrt(2), giving leading constant 4(mu_1^r/mu_1^c+1)^2 sum 1/(mu_i^c Delta_i). Comparator is the optimal policy knowing distributions (approximately always pulling the best-ratio arm). Algorithm does not need B, so recorded as anytime.
